title: Pilot traffic throttle & 30-day KPI pulse
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc for the pilot launch gating and the first-30-day KPI pulse. Focus: small-batch enterprise beta (reserved seats, dedicated infra) that needs strict traffic-throttle rules, quick rollback heuristics, and a concise metric ticker for the on-call desk.

Scope:
- Pilot cohort: 12 beta customers (invite-only), ramp across 3 waves (2, 4, 6 customers).
- Platforms: hosted API + dedicated reservation pool.
- Timeline: Pilot start (wave 1) target: 2025-02-10; full pilot closure and learnings: 2025-03-12.

Quick gist (notes to self):
- Keep throttle knobs coarse early, prefer manual gradation during first 72h.
- We must avoid automatic full-scale autoscale until wave 2 metrics stable for 48h.
- Reserve fallback path to smaller, quantized model variant for cost SLO.

Daily readiness ticker (ops desk):
- 08:00: health-check snapshot (SLO burn, 1h trend) -> posted to #pilot-ops.
- 12:00: capacity headroom check (remaining burst minutes for Dedicated pool).
- 16:00: customer-visible error rate check (5min p99 latencies).

Primary KPIs (definitions + targets for pilot):
1) Request success rate (application-level)
   - definition: % of user requests that return 2xx semantic responses (no model error, no truncation), excluding client-side timeouts.
   - pilot target: >= 99.0% daily, alert if < 98.5% for two consecutive hours.
2) P50/P90/P99 latency (in ms for token generation endpoint)
   - target: P50 < 180ms, P90 < 350ms, P99 < 700ms for hosted; Dedicated targets are 20% better.
3) Cost per 1k tokens (estimated billed unit)
   - target: within 12% of predicted budget for first 30 days; flag if > 20%.
4) Throughput headroom (reserved pool burst minutes)
   - definition: minutes of sustained peak QPS before hitting soft capacity.
   - target: min 30 minutes before manual intervention.
5) Quality drift (eval-set BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent for our prompt baseline)
   - target: no more than 2% drop vs baseline; automated eval runs daily during rollout.
6) Customer support latency (first response time for pilot tickets)
   - target: < 2 business hours, escalate if > 4 hours.

Signal thresholds and automatic actions (heuristic ladder):
- Green: All KPIs within target -> permit next wave to be invited after 48h stable.
- Amber: Any KPI in warning band (e.g., p99 > 700ms or success rate 98.0–98.5%) -> freeze automated onboarding, notify owners, open incident channel.
- Red: Major SLO breach (success rate < 98% sustained for 30m OR p99 > 1.2s) -> trigger immediate rollback to safe model variant + reduce traffic to 10% and notify exec on-call.

Traffic-throttle playbook (practical knobs):
- Soft throttle: reduce per-customer QPS cap by 50% (applied by routing-policy) -> 1st action after amber.
- Hard throttle: divert 90% of request volume to fallback model variant or cached responses -> 2nd action after 15m amber if no improvement.
- Circuit breaker: global ingress throttle to 20% of baseline traffic -> when red breach detected.

Owner map (who does what) [working, update owners in rota]:
- Traffic gating & routing: Ethan Moore (eng-platform) -> slack: @ethan / channel: #routing-ops
- Capacity & Dedicated pool ops: Lina Huang (infra) -> @lina / channel: #infra-dedicated
- Quality & Eval checks: Ravi Patel (applied-ml) -> @ravi / channel: #evals
- Customer comms & playbook lead: Marta Kovacs (cs) -> @marta / channel: #cs-pilot
- Product ops lead / triage owner: Priya Singh (product-ops) -> @priya / channel: #pilot-ops

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before wave 1 traffic unpause):
- [ ] Canary passes for 48h with no SLO breach (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Dedicated pool capacity validated with 2x expected peak QPS for 30m sustained (owner: Lina)
- [ ] Daily eval harness run integrated into pipeline and baseline metrics uploaded (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Customer welcome templates + agreed escalation path validated (owner: Marta)
- [ ] Cost dashboards populated and verified vs forecast (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Runbook pinned in Confluence + on-call rota confirmed (owner: Priya)

Post-launch 30-day pulse cadence (what to collect and when):
- Week 0 (first 7 days): hourly KPI snapshot, end-of-day incident digest.
- Week 1–2: 4x daily snapshots, quality eval daily, cost burn 2x daily.
- Week 3–4: daily snapshots, weekly deep-dive for cohort segmentation.
- Weekly debriefs: product + eng + cs (30m) every Monday; actionable items logged in JIRA.

What to watch for (risks / unknowns):
- Dependency: model-variant quantization quality may degrade some prompts we haven't caught in eval set. Action: extend eval set with customer-specific sample prompts (ask solutions-engineering to collect).
- Risk: autoscale oscillation if we unpause all customers in wave 2 -> prefer phased ramp with manual gating every 6 hours.
- Unknown: burst patterns from specific integration (e.g., webhook replay). Add integration-level throttles for first 72h.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- TODO: confirm Confluence runbook link + ensure all owners have edit rights (action item: Priya).
- TODO: add customer-specific SLAs to roster (Marta to collect).
- Question: should we enable model-variant prewarming for heavy prompt cohorts? (Ethan to prototype warm path).

Appendix: Short checklist for on-call when amber/red triggers:
1) Post summary to #pilot-ops with metrics + suspected root cause.
2) If amber, apply soft throttle, wait 15m for stabilization.
3) If no improvement or red, execute hard throttle and switch to fallback route; page eng-sre and product-ops lead.
4) Start incident timeline doc and notify customer success for impacted customers.

Links & references:
- Pilot canary runbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Pilot-Canary-Runbook
- Routing policy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-config/pull/587
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Templates

End notes (informal):
- This document intentionally pragmatic — fewer automated leaps during initial days. Keep communication tight and prefer manual roll-forward to learn fast.
- If this approach proves too conservative, we can add staged automation after week 2.

Last edits:
- 2025-02-02: tightened amber thresholds; added warm-path question (Priya)
- 2025-01-14: initial draft and owner assignments
